name: koto-collection-spread
instr:
Please add postfix spread and assignment rest targets to Koto in `/app`, to compose and take apart collections. Use the existing `koto_runtime::KotoVm::run(&mut self, chunk: Ptr<Chunk>) -> Result<KValue>` API. Don't add new crates.

In lists, parenthesized tuples, and comma tuples on an assignment's right-hand side, `xs...` inserts its iterator's values at that position, using packed-call iterable semantics. Whitespace before `...` is allowed. Ordinary elements stay unflattened, and expansion has no call-argument register limit. `(xs...)` is always a tuple. A spread alone outside a collection or call remains invalid, including `x = xs...`.

In braced maps, `{base..., f()..., key: value}` accepts arbitrary map expressions alongside ordinary and meta entries. Copy only own data entries, shallowly and in insertion order, without invoking iterator hooks. Later equal keys replace values without moving the first key's position. Source metadata is not copied; explicit destination metadata applies.

Evaluate entries once, left to right, consuming each spread completely before the next entry, even for discarded collections. Invalid operand types and iteration failures are catchable runtime errors. Catching an error must leave enclosing collection construction usable.

On assignment's left-hand side, allow one identifier or ignored target with `...`: `a, middle..., z = values` collects the middle into a tuple, with fixed targets taking values from the beginning and end. `all... = value
